hints.title: Quadruplet Deduplication Search Obstacle
hints.text: Examining all quadruplets takes quartic time and produces duplicate sets. If you sort the array and fix the first two values, how can you find the remaining pairs in linear time while bypassing duplicates?

hints.title: Two-Level Fix with Inward Pointer Sweep
hints.text: Fix the first two numbers using nested loops, then use converging markers on the remaining subarray to identify matching pair sums while skipping duplicate values at every level.

hints.title: Dual Fixed Indices with Inward Sweep Procedure
hints.text: Sort the array. Run index i from 0 to n minus 4 and index j from i plus 1 to n minus 3, skipping identical values to avoid duplicates. Set left to j plus 1 and right to n minus 1. Compute the four-element sum using 64-bit integers. If equal to target, record the quadruplet and advance past identical values. If below target, step left forward; otherwise step right backward.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of nums array (1 <= N <= 200)
complexity.notes: O(N^3) sorted two-pointer sweep with O(1) auxiliary space beyond the output list.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Evaluating all combinations takes O(N^4) time, resulting in ~1.6 * 10^9 operations for N=200 and hitting Time Limit Exceeded.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting upfront enables skipping duplicates in O(1) memory and brings complexity from quartic O(N^4) down to O(N^3).
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Preventing 32-bit signed integer overflow when summing 4 large integers by casting to 64-bit (long long in C++, long in Java).
